_: Every number the compressor lesson says. MEASURED off renders on 2026-09-04, never assumed. Predictions in predict.py were written BEFORE any of it was rendered.

material.tone: one held A3 sine from the poly synth, 7.5 beats at 100 BPM
material.drums: kick/snare/hat programmed note by note from sine + square. No sample is loaded anywhere.

d1_threshold_and_ratio._: over = 12 dB by construction (threshold derived from the MEASURED dry peak), hard knee, so the prediction is the plain ratio line.

d1b_why_it_is_not_exactly_9._: ⭐ THE BEST BEAT IN THE EPISODE AND IT WAS NOT PLANNED. The static curve is an idealisation; the detector is a PEAK follower that decays between the peaks of the wave, so steady-state reduction falls slightly short. CONFIRMED by three points, not asserted: the shortfall closes monotonically as release lengthens.

d2_attack._: Same drum hit, same everything, only attackMs changes. Attack is not 'how fast it works' — it is HOW MUCH OF THE TRANSIENT YOU KEEP.

d3_release._: RE-DESIGNED 2026-09-05: release is PREDICTED, not compared. The first cut measured the output envelope of a drum loop and reported 6.45 Hz for fast release, slow release AND the bypassed control — that rate was the drum pattern, and the figure was retracted. Release is exactly as predictable as threshold and knee.
d3_release.formula: CompressorEffect.swift:184 — releaseCoeff = exp(-1/(releaseMs*0.001*sampleRate)) is a one-pole with tau = releaseMs, so from G dB of reduction the time back to within 1 dB of unity is t = releaseMs * ln(G). From 12 dB: ln(12) = 2.4849.
d3_release.material: A GATED BURST, not the drum loop: a loop cannot show a release because the next hit arrives before the recovery finishes. A4 for two beats over a quiet A3 tail 25.5 dB below it.
d3_release.why_a_tail_and_not_silence: Gain is measured as compressed/dry SAMPLE BY SAMPLE (mix 1, makeup 0, so comp[i] = dry[i]*gain[i] exactly). On silence that division is 0/0. The tail is the carrier the recovery is measured ON, and at 12.7 dB below the threshold the compressor's target is exactly 0 throughout it.
d3_release.settings: threshold = burst peak - 14.5 dB, ratio 20, hard knee, attack 1 ms, makeup 0, mix 1
d3_release.measured_from: the gain crossing -12 dB to the gain crossing -1 dB, each crossing LINEARLY INTERPOLATED between the samples that bracket it — a TWO-CROSSING time, which does not depend on where the burst ended or on how deep the reduction went

control_ratio1._: ⭐ THE CONTROL THAT MAKES IT FALSIFIABLE. Same burst, ratio 1:1 — no reduction to recover from, so the recovery time must be undefined.

d3_release.deviation_and_its_named_cause: ⚠⚠ RETRACTED WITHIN THE SAME RE-CUT, AND THE RETRACTION IS NOW THE BEAT. The first pass measured 74.688 ms at a 30 ms release and attributed the 0.2 ms overshoot to the detector's fixed 5 ms peak decay (CompressorEffect.swift:140). THAT WAS THE INSTRUMENT, NOT THE COMPRESSOR: the gain curve discarded every sample within FLOOR_DB of a zero crossing, and against a -39.67 dBFS tail a -60 dB floor blanks ~0.15 ms per half cycle — which finds the -12 crossing EARLY and the -1 crossing LATE, both biases pointing long. At a -80 dB floor it reads 74.583; with both crossings interpolated, 74.57 against a 74.55 prediction, a residual of 0.02 ms. The detector's decay IS real and IS still falling when the release starts — it simply CANCELS between two crossings, because after the target reaches 0 the envelope is a pure exponential. ⭐ CONTROL YOUR METRIC BEFORE YOU EXPLAIN A NUMBER IT PRODUCED — the same lesson that retracted the 6.45 Hz figure, one layer deeper.
d3_release.first_attempt_retained_as_evidence: The first pass set the reduction to 12.2 dB and the 30 ms release NEVER REACHED -12 (deepest -11.934) — a fast release starts recovering while the peak detector is still falling. Deepening to 13.8 dB makes the -12 crossing exist at every release; the two-crossing time is independent of depth.

d4_knee._: The demo nobody does: a tone 2 dB BELOW threshold. A hard knee is not working at all; a soft knee already is.

d5_makeup._: Why every compressor A/B you have heard is a lie. Gentle 3:1, soft knee — the setting a mix engineer actually reaches for.
d5_makeup.surprise_peak_note: ⭐ AT EQUAL LOUDNESS the compressed take PEAKS 4.5 dB HIGHER (-6.09 vs -10.59 dBFS): a 10 ms attack passes the transient, then makeup lifts it. Compression did not reduce the peaks — it raised them. This is why a limiter follows a compressor.

d6_mix._: Parallel ('New York') compression: density back without flattening the transient — impossible fully wet.

bit_exact_bypass_at_mix0._: The docs CLAIM mix:0 is a bit-exact bypass. VERIFIED three ways rather than repeated.

d6_mix.ab_is_unlevelled: ⭐ CHANGED 2026-09-05: the A/B is NO LONGER loudness-levelled. The levelled version put the 19.3 LU collapse on a card while only the transient half was audible — a number on screen the ear could not check. One shared static gain (+12.581 dB, chosen from the louder file's peak) is applied to both halves, so the 19.3 LU really plays.
